items.summary: Cisco, an enterprise technology services company operating globally and in North America under its Daybreak product line, describes integrating OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model. Cisco states the combination represents a step function improvement to security posture, enabling defenders to operate at machine speed and scale.
items.title: Cisco Deploys OpenAI Models for Machine-Speed Security Defense

items.summary: A forthcoming complaint seen by Reuters alleges Tesla misled South Korean buyers of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software for years, collecting lump-sum payments while the technology worked on only about 20% of Teslas sold there. A KFTC probe is underway; consumer groups seek fines and a cease-and-desist order.
items.title: Tesla Faces South Korean Complaint Over FSD Marketing

items.summary: AMD forecast more than 80 per cent revenue growth in 2027, above analysts' estimate of 77 per cent, as data-center sales surged to a record $8.55 billion and its challenge to Nvidia gathered pace. Shares rose 8 per cent. CEO Lisa Su cited demand across CPU and AI businesses. Client and gaming sales fell 8 per cent to $3.72 billion, missing estimates of $3.79 billion.
items.title: AMD Eases AI Spending Fears With Data-Center Sales Surge

items.summary: As OpenAI moves into developing its own data centers amid growing public backlash over electricity costs, the company announced a non-binding Grid Protection Program to support affordable and reliable power where it builds campuses. The effort relies on demand response and facility-level flexibility, with utility companies and regulators reducing energy during storms or extreme heat. In Effingham County, Georgia, OpenAI contracted with Georgia Power for 3.2 gigawatts of power, beginning operations in phases starting in 2028 under a 25-year agreement that lets the utility cut supply to create demand response capacity up to a GW. The company frames flexibility as central to its design and operation nationwide. Industry group Edison Electric Institute notes growing interest in flexible large loads, while pollsters track rising voter concern ahead of midterms on data center impacts.
items.title: OpenAI Pledges Grid-Friendly Power Use as Data Center Backlash Grows

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India amended the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) regulations, effective October 1, 2026. Resident individuals exporting services are now deemed to have submitted an Export Declaration Form once their payment is credited by a bank, with no transaction-value threshold set for them. For other exporters, the form counts as filed if inward remittance stays at or below Rs 10 lakh. On service imports, banks must enter details in IDPMS when the importer is not a resident individual and the invoice value exceeds Rs 10 lakh, within five working days of receipt.
items.title: RBI Eases Forex Rules for Services Exports and Imports

items.summary: Canva Inc announced job cuts and role changes affecting more than one-fifth of its staff, with about 1,271 people impacted. CEO Melanie Perkins said the firm’s growth slowed for the first time in a decade as artificial intelligence reshapes work. She called it the hardest moment in Canva’s 13-year history but did not specify how many would lose their jobs.
items.title: Canva Cuts Jobs for About a Fifth of Its Workforce Amid Slowdown

items.summary: Google says it will let educators choose whether to allow its AI tools in the classroom, with administrators able to manually enable them as changes roll out over coming months. However, blocking these tools also means giving up Google Search, leaving schools facing a difficult decision between allowing all AI features or none of them.
items.title: Google's AI opt-out forces schools to abandon search too

items.summary: An adviser to the Court of Justice of the EU said Tuesday that Google's AI chatbot Gemini could violate press publishers' rights by retrieving and reusing online news articles. First Advocate General Maciej Szpunar delivered the opinion in a case brought by Hungarian media company Like Company against Google Ireland, alleging Gemini reproduced their content so users need not access originals.
items.title: EU court adviser warns Google Gemini may breach press copyright

items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team released FlashProve, an open-source zkSNARK prototype that proves a reply came from committed model weights without revealing them. On Llama 4 Maverick (a ~400B mixture-of-experts model), it achieves about 110 tokens/second on one H100 GPU; proofs are roughly 18.78 MB and verify in 17 seconds on a CPU. Anthropic says this targets the gap where users cannot confirm which model answered an API call, offering use cases for regulators and tamper detection. Proving costs about 70 to 95x plain vLLM inference GPU time. The protocol is formalized in Lean with post-quantum security claims; Claude reportedly helped optimize it.
items.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve for Provable AI Inference

items.summary: The 2026 NEMO User Meeting, hosted by MIT.nano Oct. 5–6 and sponsored by the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition (NEMC) hub, gathered 65 representatives from 25 laboratories and organizations to share approaches to lab management. The event centered on the NanoFab Equipment Management and Operations (NEMO) system, an open-source platform used across diverse facilities with similar operational challenges. Anna Osherov, associate director of Characterization.nano and meeting organizer, emphasized collaboration as a key strength. MIT.nano alone supports more than 1,600 active researchers using more than 200 tools, with approximately 160,000 hours of tool usage each year.
items.title: MIT.nano Hosts Meeting on Shared Research Infrastructure

items.summary: The Netherlands’ RDW confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping Tesla’s driver-assistance system’s speed margin at 10% over the limit, down from 50%, in Europe. The regulator also officially renamed “FSD Supervised” to “Tesla Assisted Driving,” saying the change does not alter what the system does and that the driver remains responsible. On a 100 km/h highway the old margin allowed up to 150 km/h; now it tops out at +10%. The update lands weeks before EU member states vote on bloc-wide approval, which is pushed to December and requires a qualified majority of 15 of 27 states. Germany’s backing came after Tesla agreed to drop the name and cap speed tolerance at 10%, conditions Sweden still opposes by demanding no setting above the limit. The RDW notified nine member states recognizing its approval: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia.
items.title: Tesla Cuts European Speed Margin and Renames FSD

items.summary: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45% year over year, as its Data Center segment rose 97% to a record $8.5 billion. Adjusted earnings were $2.09 per share versus $1.20 a year earlier. CEO Lisa Su said the company expects growth to accelerate in the fourth quarter amid production scaling of Helios systems and Venice processors, forecasting about $17 billion plus or minus 3%.
items.title: AMD Beats Earnings Estimates on Record Data Center Revenue

items.summary: OpenAI started giving Indian users a free year of ChatGPT Go on 4 November 2025, so the earliest trials end around 4 November 2026. The length is reported as twelve months from signup day, though this could not be confirmed by checked reports. A December cutoff was unconfirmed too. Renewals reportedly cost ₹399 a month unless cancelled; subscriptions bill automatically and may auto-save payment methods.
items.title: OpenAI's Free ChatGPT Go Trial May End Soon for Indian Users

items.summary: Deepinder Goyal, founder of Zomato, says his ₹85,000 Temple wearable beat five flagship trackers, including the Apple Watch Series 12, in a company-run heart rate accuracy test detailed in an October 31 research paper. He urges sceptical buyers to wait for independent testing even as pre-orders open in India.
items.title: Zomato Founder Claims Temple Beats Apple Watch in Heart Rate Test

items.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a petition questioning whether an Uttar Pradesh additional district judge, chargesheeted by Delhi Police under Section 376 IPC for allegedly raping a woman met on a matrimonial site, can head a Pocso court. A bench issued notice and sought the Allahabad High Court's response.
items.title: Supreme Court Reviews Judge Presiding Over Pocso Case While Facing Rape Chargesheet

items.summary: A 12-member expert committee reviewing the NEET-PG process told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that the National Medical Commission is working to replace percentile-based counselling with a rank-based system for NEET-PG and Super Speciality admissions. The proposal received in-principle approval at an NMC meeting on Sept 23, per a letter dated Oct 1, but regulations remain unfinalised as courts examine petitions over reduced qualifying cut-offs.
items.title: NMC Panel Approves Rank-Based System for NEET PG Admissions

items.summary: US Treasury yields rose as robust September job openings and falling layoffs reinforced confidence in a resilient economy, pushing the benchmark 10 year yield to 4.954% per Reuters data. Yields briefly eased after oil fell following President Trump's comments about cutting Israel funding but recovered on fresh economic strength. Sage Advisory's Thomas Urano said yields are repricing higher amid unambiguously strong data and resilient growth, while investors stayed cautious ahead of midterm election results that could shape fiscal policy and Treasury supply.
items.title: Treasury yields climb on strong jobs data and midterm polls

items.summary: Polls closed across Florida, Georgia, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia, North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia on election night. Associated Press exit poll data shows the economy (39%) and state of democracy (32%) top voter concerns, with roughly 60% disapproving of Trump’s presidency. Voters in Austin, Texas; Rochester, New Hampshire; Linn County, Kansas; and Fort Lupton, Colorado shared cost-of-living worries and Democratic hopes as results streamed in.
items.title: US midterm elections 2026 live updates: polls close in some key states as Americans deliver referendum on Trump’s second term

items.summary: Canva announced a shake-up affecting about one in five workers, including job losses, relocations and role changes. Co-founder Melanie Perkins called it the hardest moment in the company's thirteen-year history. The firm reportedly saw its value fall as worries grew over artificial intelligence's impact on its business and rising AI costs. Sydney will become the primary home for more product teams.
items.title: Canva cuts jobs after hardest year yet amid AI concerns

items.summary: Recent UK graduates are increasingly taking on dedicated artificial intelligence roles, with some managing numerous agents and handling responsibilities they would normally reach only after several years. Employers such as ArvCConnect's CEO Debra Maxwell say the trend can build more engaged staff, though she has paused graduate hiring this year to refocus next intake on AI-disruptor positions. Consultancy PwC found that entry-level roles influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to demand senior skills and have grown 35% since 2019, while other such roles shrank by 10%. Critics including Portman Finance Group's Simon Pratt warn over-reliance on AI risks graduates neglecting core professional training. PwC UK's Claire Reed adds that baseline AI literacy is now unavoidable but must be paired with sector knowledge for long-term career progression.
items.title: UK graduates lean into AI while worrying about lost trade skills

items.summary: United Overseas Bank (UOB) reported a third-quarter net profit of $1.25 billion, up 182% from $443 million a year earlier, the bank said on Nov 4. The rise came mainly from lower provisions for potential loan losses: UOB set aside $258 million in the quarter ended Sept 30, down 81% from $1.36 billion a year earlier. Net profit fell 15% from $1.48 billion over the previous quarter and missed a $1.38 billion forecast among six analysts polled by Bloomberg. Fee income hit a record $733 million, up 19% on the prior year.
items.title: UOB Reports Sharp Q3 Profit Jump on Lower Loan Loss Provisions

items.summary: ZDNET reports Apple cannot predict when its foldable iPhone Duo will reach supply–demand balance, with shipping delays extending to 2027. On an earnings call Monday Nov. 2, chief operating officer Sabih Khan said the company could not forecast when stock would meet demand. CEO John Ternus cited strong early customer response and a deepened partnership with titanium producer Perryman.
items.title: Apple's iPhone Duo supply struggles may delay holiday sales into 2027

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple's Siri Recap and Live Rewind, two always-listening Audio Intelligence features on the Series 12 and Ultra 4 smartwatches running iOS 27.3 developer beta, are now available to try. Both remain opt-in. Siri Recap summarizes conversations into notes focused on key takeaways rather than full transcripts, while Live Rewind transcribes the last 15 seconds of audio after a double-press of the Digital Crown. Apple describes its Secure Exclave as processing audio privately without sending it to Apple, and says both features are off by default according to Apple. The author notes they have not tested some controls themselves.
items.title: Apple Watch Adds Two Controversial Listening Features in Beta

items.summary: NVIDIA reports that three stacked optimizations lift GSM8K decode throughput for the Ling-3.0-flash model 42.5% on a single DGX Spark desktop system, from 37.81 to 53.89 tokens per second. The techniques are Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels, an online FP8 LM head and built-in MTP speculative decoding with NEXTN. NVIDIA says accuracy moved only from 96.89% to 96.82%, a change it calls statistically undetectable, while mean latency fell about 24.5%. The team notes the model is memory-bound at batch size one and that stacking FP8 LM head with MTP requires sharing the full LM-head module or throughput drops below baseline.
items.title: NVIDIA Boosts MoE Inference Speed on DGX Spark

items.summary: Researchers at Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant analyzed incidents of LLMjacking, where stolen API keys drive fraudulent cloud AI usage. They identified two threat-actor clusters that compromise enterprise infrastructure and resell access through services like Jet Night and newapi[.]pro. Fraudulent charges reached $1 million in some cases, with daily losses exceeding $100,000 at affected organizations. Google recommends strengthening IAM controls, rotating secrets, enforcing MFA, setting spending limits, and monitoring logs to detect such attacks early.
items.title: Google: LLMjacking attacks rack up $1 million in cloud AI charges

items.summary: Apple announced new App Store rules requiring dating and romantic apps, including those with sexual or romantic content, to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers must add content descriptors so age ratings reflect app features. The policy follows broader child-safety changes Apple has rolled out globally.
items.title: Apple Bars Minors From Dating and AI Companion Apps

items.summary: Databricks introduced UNIQUE constraints in Public Preview for Unity Catalog Delta tables, available in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 18.2 or above. Unlike the single PRIMARY KEY, which requires non-nullable columns, a table can declare multiple UNIQUE constraints whose columns may be nullable, and foreign keys can reference them. After validation with RELY, the query optimizer—on Photon-enabled compute—can eliminate unnecessary joins and aggregations. Benchmarks on TPC-DS SF10000 (a 10 TB scale factor) showed join elimination removing more than 99.99% of shuffle and cutting median execution time from 23.6 seconds to 3.0 seconds, a 7.9x speedup; DISTINCT aggregation removal cut time from 33.7 seconds to 2.8 seconds, a 12.0x speedup. Constraints are informational by default (NORELY) and not enforced on writes; RELY should be used only for validated guarantees.
items.title: Databricks Adds UNIQUE Constraints for Query Optimization

items.summary: In its fiscal-year filing ending Sept. 26, Apple says autonomous AI agents could operate independently—entering systems without permission, running code, sending messages and finalizing purchases—and may exceed permissions or be manipulated by malicious inputs. The company notes it has no agentic product yet but faces reputational, regulatory and legal risks as the technology spreads.
items.title: Apple Warns AI Agents May Act Without Authorization

items.summary: Tech Policy Press editor Amber Sinha frames Elon Musk's public complaint about Starlink as a clash between Silicon Valley platform power and India's domestic telecom conglomerates. Musk accused unnamed Indian entities of a monopolistic chokehold, questioning whether Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani was the real boss of India. The article notes New Delhi codified administrative spectrum assignment for satellite services in 2023 favoring Starlink, yet authorization remains stalled in security vetting overseen by the Ministry of Home Affairs. It traces Reliance's history of regulatory maneuvering and cites a TRAI Interconnection Usage Charge cut of 57% in 2017. Sinha argues India may also weigh national-security concerns over LEO constellations, pointing to Taiwan's requirement that domestic entities hold at least 51% stakes.
items.title: Starlink Founder Blames Indian Oligarchs Over Spectrum Access

items.summary: Canva is cutting or relocating more than 1,200 jobs, about 22% of its global workforce. CEO Melanie Perkins said the restructure was “without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history”. The company says it will affect 1,271 people as it collapses layers and brings teams together in person. Departing staff receive at least six months’ salary and can apply for US$10,000 startup grants.
items.title: Canva cuts or relocates over 1,200 jobs in restructuring

items.summary: South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's former ruling party, the African National Congress. The party had lost its parliamentary majority at the last national election and support has dropped from 70% in 2004 to 40%. President Cyril Ramaphosa denied his party was in decline, telling supporters they would show naysayers on the 4th of November. Analysts say polls point to a continued fall for the ANC and rising support for the Democratic Alliance. In Alexandra township residents cite poor service delivery; an Auditor-General report found only 39 clean audits between 2024 and 2025, with none of Gauteng's metros included. Political analysts Melanie Verwoerd and Dr Levy Ndou expect coalitions to remain common across Gauteng as voters weigh governance failures against change.
items.title: South African voters weigh ANC's grip on local governance amid decline

items.summary: Kim Kardashian said she will retake the California bar exam, aiming to become a lawyer in real life after playing one on Hulu's legal drama All's Fair. She discovered she had failed following the show's first series last year, having studied law for six years beforehand. Speaking with BBC's Annabel Rackham ahead of the program's second series, Kardashian said: 'I'll take it again and let you guys know once I've passed.'
items.title: Kim Kardashian Plans to Retake California Bar Exam

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that Washington would end its annual aid to Israel, citing a deal made months earlier and criticism from Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Under the arrangement, Israel received roughly US$3.8 billion yearly for weapons purchases. Netanyahu was reported as accepting the decision; opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot called it evidence Netanyahu must go. The move came amid midterm elections in the United States.
items.title: Trump Announces End of Annual US Aid to Israel

items.summary: More than a week after unexpectedly defeating Aleksandar Vucic at the polls, Serbia's incoming student-led bloc has not yet taken its parliamentary seats or named a prime minister. Meanwhile, officials in Belgrade that Vucic dominated for over a decade have begun dismantling his regime: leaders at institutions such as the central bank and state prosecutors office have called for investigations into potential crimes during his tenure, while top brass from the state broadcaster resigned or apologized for biased coverage.
items.title: Serbia's leaderless bloc begins dismantling Vucic regime

items.summary: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he had reached a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after this year, though weapons sales will continue. He framed the move as removing a Democratic talking point ahead of midterm elections. Trump did not provide details on how the funding would be halted, noting the Memorandum of Understanding providing $3.8 billion expires only in September 2028.
items.title: Trump Announces Halting of $4 Billion in U.S. Aid to Israel

items.summary: From November 1, Sebi requires mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their websites and apps, pre-selecting them for equity investments. The change aims to lower costs by reducing commissions paid to distributors that raise regular-plan expense ratios. Investors can still choose regular plans with distributor assistance.
items.title: Sebi Makes Direct Mutual Fund Plans Default From November

items.summary: Amanda Serrano wants to be remembered as a game changer ahead of her farewell fight against Skye Falzon on January 9 at Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan. The seven-division world champion will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight titles in a bout dubbed 'The Last Walk.' She owns a 50-4-1 record with 32 knockouts, and she is the first undisputed women's world champion from Puerto Rico.
items.title: Serrano Aims for Legacy as Farewell Bout Approaches

items.summary: A new satellite tracking system called the Forest Monitor tool finds that the United States lost about 350,000 acres of forest land per year from 1990 to 2017, roughly one football field every two minutes. Researchers at Clark University announced the initial findings Thursday through Inside Climate News. The tool tracks persistent loss in the lower 48 states and shows 9.8 million acres lost to development or agriculture over that span—about 2 percent of total U.S. forestland across 28 years, equivalent to roughly 2.3 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions. Lead author Christopher Williams noted Southeast losses were especially dramatic, with Georgia most affected.
items.title: Satellite Tool Reveals Rapid U.S. Forest Loss

items.summary: Block raised its full-year gross profit outlook after strength in its Cash App unit lifted quarterly earnings and the company reached a preliminary settlement with the US Department of Justice over its anti-money laundering program. Shares rose 7 per cent in extended trading as Block expects $12.63 billion in gross profit for 2026, up from its prior forecast of $12.51 billion.
items.title: Block Raises Full-Year Profit Outlook on Cash App, Reaches Preliminary DOJ Deal

items.summary: David Hume Kennerly, a Pulitzer-prize-winning photographer with decades of experience, discusses photographing election night. He notes that photographers position themselves ready to capture history-making moments during these events.
items.title: Legendary Photographer Shares Tips on Capturing Election Night Images

items.summary: As the Ukraine war continues, relations between Russia and Japan have reached their worst in decades. Tokyo is seeking greater support from Washington, though some Japanese officials worry it may not come.
items.title: Japan Weighs U.S. Support Amid Pressure From Nuclear Neighbors

items.summary: US tech stocks rebounded on Tuesday after a selloff driven by concerns over AI spending. The S&P 500 rose 0.37% and the Nasdaq climbed 0.83%, while the Dow fell 0.37%. Nvidia gained 2.3%, though Apple dropped as its margin forecast missed expectations due to memory chip costs. Brent crude eased on Iran-Russia talks, adding relief. The recovery followed October's sharpest monthly decline since March 2025.
items.title: Tech Stocks Recover After AI Spending Fears

items.summary: Kalyn Ponga is expected to return for New Zealand just 22 days after breaking his left arm, ahead of the World Cup clash against Tonga. He must pass fitness tests during the week to be cleared to play. Ponga and Phoenix Crossland have been named on NZ's extended bench for Saturday night's match.
items.title: Ponga Aims for Quick Return Ahead of Tonga Clash

items.summary: Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente announced his resignation six days after a high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 69 people. Authorities closed the search and returned remains to families, with all victims identified. Two Australians were among 15 foreign nationals killed. Mr Puente called it the second serious crash in under a year and said safety measures would follow, including better control centres and faster rollout of European Rail Traffic Management System. The October 28 crash occurred after communication systems failed on the Madrid-Seville line. Concerns about rail safety have grown ahead of an election.
items.title: Spain's Transport Minister Resigns After Deadly High-Speed Train Crash

items.summary: An initial assessment released by Binance on Tuesday attributes the world's biggest-ever cyber heist, which stole over $6 billion worth of customer crypto last week, to a North Korean military unit called TraderTraitor. The FBI identified the group as responsible for attacks that may have taken about twenty minutes but were months in preparation.
items.title: Binance Blames North Korean Hackers for Record Heist

items.summary: Researchers spotted the Ghana cuckooshrike in Côte d'Ivoire's Taï National Park, ending its absence from records since 2013. Stephanie Bartlett of the International Bird Conservation Partnership captured an identifying photo while Paulo Ditzel guided her by calling out the bird's movements. The species had not been documented for over a decade and could have gone extinct or remained hidden in forest canopy.
items.title: Photograph Identifies West African Bird Absent for Over a Decade

items.summary: Mark Warner won re-election to the US Senate in Virginia, defeating Republican Bert Mizusawa. Polls closed across more states at 7:30PM ET and again later that evening in six states including Florida, Georgia, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia. Around a third of the Senate's 100 seats are up for election, with Republicans currently holding 53 to Democrats' 45 amid two independents.
items.title: Warner wins Virginia Senate seat as US midterms polls close

items.summary: A programme called Tech Life reports that independent journalists worldwide are falling victim to fake copyright strikes against their content on social media, particularly when their stories criticize powerful figures. The episode also covers how AI has been integrated into safety measures on US railroads and technology helping a live orchestra stay in sync with Lord of the Rings screenings.
items.title: Journalists targeted by fake copyright strikes on social media

items.summary: The first midterm votes counted Tuesday night suggest a difficult night for Republicans, consistent with polling placing Democrats ahead on frustration with President Donald Trump’s agenda. In Indiana and Kentucky, where polls closed at 6 pm ET, Democrats led their early totals two years ago. Both seats saw later investment as the environment worsened for Republicans; House Majority PAC spent nearly $400,000 in Indiana while a green energy group backed its opponent. Democrats remain cautious about overreading early returns after losing ground on Election Day previously.
items.title: Early Midterm Votes Show Democrats Ahead in Indiana and Kentucky

items.summary: India's external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated calls for dialogue after the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island, saying hostilities have disrupted global fuel, food and fertiliser flows. The conflict has killed 23 Indian nationals, including seafarers aboard MSV Al Jusufi off Oman, where 13 of 14 were rescued. India also cited concerns for over 10 million Indians in the region and urged freedom of navigation to be restored.
items.title: India Urges Dialogue as West Asia Conflict Deepens Toll on Energy and Lives

items.summary: Punjab’s Tarn Taran district authorities registered 240 FIRs against farmers and imposed about Rs 12 lakh in fines this season for stubble burning. The revenue department marked 240 fields with red entries, while satellite monitoring flagged 400 suspected locations; of these, burning was confirmed at 215 sites and not confirmed at 245. District Agriculture Officer Tejbir Singh Bhangu said teams are visiting villages to promote crop-residue management as incidents persist despite enforcement.
items.title: Tarn Taran Registers Hundreds of FIRs in Stubble-Burning Crackdown

items.summary: The Indian Navy has begun court-martial proceedings against two officers over alleged lapses that led to the locally built guided-missile frigate INS Brahmaputra partially capsizing at a Naval Dockyard in Mumbai during repairs. The commanding officer, a captain, faces charges of hazarding a naval ship and negligence; the officer of the day, a lieutenant commander, has been charged with negligence. A sailor was killed when a fire broke out on July 2024 while crews pumped water to control the blaze. The frigate remains under trials and is expected to be seaworthy next year. Officials said safety measures from a special task force have since been implemented.
items.title: Indian Navy Court-Martial Officers Over Frigate Capsizing

items.summary: Supermarket fridges and freezers in several European countries malfunctioned after a reported cyber-attack that remotely raised their thermostats. It is unclear who is behind the apparent attack, but the EU condemned it as 'a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply.' Separately, the UK's cybersecurity body warns AI-powered malicious software may target power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028.
items.title: EU Condemns Cyber-Attack on European Supermarket Fridges and Freezers

items.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes damaged Russian data centers housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of users. In response, the Kremlin requires operators to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and authorized possible use of foreign facilities. State-owned Rostelcom raised moving some centers underground in talks with Norilsk, while a regional governor proposed building them inside open-pit coal mines camouflaged by parks.
items.title: Russian Firms Plan Underground Data Centers After Ukrainian Drone Strikes

items.summary: Binance revealed that hackers behind its $6.3bn (£4.7bn) heist used fake job interviews, malware and an internal AI tool to infiltrate the exchange in October. The breach began with an inadvertent malware download in June, followed by a recruitment scam in September and a raid on hot wallets last week. Binance said $2.85bn of the $6.34bn drained had been frozen or intercepted. The FBI blames North Korea, which called the accusation “absurd rhetoric.”
items.title: Binance Discloses How Hackers Stole $6.3bn via Fake Interviews and Malware

items.summary: Rachel Curtis smelled hydrogen sulfide near her grandmother’s Odessa home and learned the nearby pumpjack is operated by Aghorn Operating. The company had pleaded guilty in 2019 to negligent endangerment and willful safety violations tied to the deaths of Jacob Dean and his wife Natalee, paying a $1 million fine; its vice president was sentenced to five months in prison. Curtis said she felt both Aghorn and authorities should monitor facilities more closely. In one case near neighbor Adrianna Yanez’s home, inspectors found leaking gas but resolved it with no penalty after the company patched it. The article notes a pattern of chronic leaks without punishment and cites calls from lawmakers for stronger oversight.
items.title: Aghorn Faces Little Penalty for Ongoing Hydrogen Sulfide Leaks After Couple's Death

items.summary: Three Nasa astronauts, including Anil Menon, cast ballots in the November 3 US midterm elections aboard the International Space Station. Menon posted a video showing his sleeping compartment used as a polling booth and said he filled out an electronic ballot sent to Harris County election officials. Fellow crew members Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins voted through the same process.
items.title: Nasa astronaut Anil Menon votes from space in US midterms

items.summary: During a Fox News interview on Election Day, Donald Trump joked that he would move to Israel and become prime minister if Americans grew tired of him. He claimed a 99 per cent approval rating there but offered no polling evidence. His remarks came as the US held midterms on November 3, with Republicans holding narrow majorities in both chambers.
items.title: Trump Jokes About Moving to Israel Amid Midterm Uncertainty

items.summary: The Royal Spanish Academy named the Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas winner of the Cervantes Prize 2026, described as the highest distinction in Spanish-language literature and worth 125,000 euros. Minister of Culture Ernest Urtasun announced the jury's decision on Tuesday, recognizing her contribution to renewing contemporary short fiction. She becomes the seventh woman awarded the prize.
items.title: Cristina Fernández Cubas Named Winner of Cervantes Prize 2026

items.summary: A global diesel shortage is expected to extend well into 2027, analysts say. Asian crude oil imports reached pre-war levels in October at 26.39 million bpd, yet gasoline and especially diesel imports from the Middle East have fallen sharply after reduced refining capacity since the Iran war began in late February. Lower refined flows through the Strait of Hormuz combined with Russian supply losses pushed refining margins to record highs by mid-2026. IEA data put global gasoil and diesel exports at 4.7 million barrels over the first nine months, down 10% year on year. Morgan Stanley added that unusually high spring maintenance could keep markets tight until next summer.
items.title: Analysts Warn Diesel Shortage May Persist Until 2027

items.summary: The war on Iran has doubled what Egypt pays for imported liquefied natural gas, according to Asharq Bloomberg. Cairo is deferring cargoes into 2027 and burning fuel oil in power plants to hold down the bill. A government official told Asharq Bloomberg that a single LNG cargo price rose as much as 100% since September, to more than $100 million. QatarEnergy has kept deliveries under force majeure since April, extending it on October 28 to end of December. Egypt’s own output fell to 3.63 bcf/d in August as older fields declined faster than new wells came online. The petroleum ministry extended the deadline for bids on 14 exploration blocks to December 14 after companies asked for more time, part of a five-year plan aiming at self-sufficiency by 2030.
items.title: Egypt Defers LNG Cargoes and Burns Fuel Oil as Iran War Doubles Gas Bill

items.summary: Average US gas prices exceeded $4 a gallon for the first time on an election day, marking a political concern for President Trump's party. Semafor's Liz Hoffman noted that whoever wins Congress inherits significant economic problems over the next two years.
items.title: US Gas Prices Reach Election Day Record of $4 a Gallon

items.summary: US air safety investigators say parts of the private jet that crashed in Florida on Sunday, killing nine people, were found miles from the impact site. Most of the Learjet 60's left elevator was recovered in three pieces between about 1.3 and 3.8 miles away, suggesting it broke off before landing. The NTSB is still determining whether losing the piece contributed to the crash.
items.title: NTSB Finds Learjet Parts Miles From Florida Crash Site

items.summary: Almost half of Ireland's corporation tax haul comes from just three companies: Apple, Eli Lilly and Microsoft. The item points readers to a fuller FT analysis by Jude Webber on why Ireland does not always feel or operate like a wealthy country.
items.title: Three Companies Make Up Nearly Half of Ireland's Tax Revenue

items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices forecast fourth-quarter revenue of US$17 billion, above the average analyst estimate of US$16.3 billion, citing accelerating growth in its data centre portfolio. The outlook offered a positive signal for investors amid concerns about an AI bubble. Shares rose about 6% in late trading after chief financial officer Jean Hu said demand across the company's data centre business remained strong.
items.title: AMD beats revenue estimates as AI chip demand stays strong

items.summary: Former OpenAI employees said they were not surprised when the company disclosed in October that it found a recording device planted in an executive conference room. According to five people familiar with the matter, staffers raised security concerns internally before ChatGPT launched in late 2022 and shared them with top leaders and the board.
items.title: OpenAI Employees Warned About Security Lapses for Years, Sources Say

items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices recorded a $1.07 billion non-cash charge, or 66 cents a share, in the third quarter ended September 26 to account for warrants it granted to customers OpenAI and Meta Platforms under chip-sale agreements. The warrants could let each customer buy up to roughly 10 per cent of AMD if milestones are met. Analysts called the deals a vote of confidence but said they were unlikely to dent Nvidia's dominance.
items.title: AMD's equity-linked deals with OpenAI and Meta trigger $1.07 billion charge

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms has held talks with Comcast and Charter Communications about licensing its wireless broadband technology, which runs on unlicensed Wi-Fi frequencies. Two people familiar with the matter said a deal could involve stakes in those companies, but no timetable exists. Jio also discussed terms with South Africa's MTN Group before talks broke down over valuation. The company listed last week after a record $3.2 billion IPO and is targeting 10 to 15 global partners for its technology platform. Comcast and Charter declined to comment; the financial details remain unclear.
items.title: Jio in Talks for US Broadband Technology Deal

items.summary: Alphabet announced that K-12 students using Google Search will have its built-in AI features enabled by default until administrators opt out, alongside Gemini tools. The change follows pushback from parents and districts over classroom AI use.
items.title: Google Requires Schools to Enable AI in Search

items.summary: The authors converted Apple's Indian launch prices into take-home pay terms, using ₹25,000 monthly as the base. On that measure, the iPhone 18 Pro equals about 6.6 months and the foldable iPhone 12 months; MacBook Pros equal roughly 14 to 23.6 months. The authors note real costs would extend this further.
items.title: Apple's India prices equal months of a fresh graduate salary

items.summary: Google ran an AI model aboard a prototype satellite in orbit, generating responses without ground computers. The demonstration used one of Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) installed under Project Suncatcher. The system received a command from Earth, processed it in orbit and sent back an AI-generated answer. While the first task was a simple poem, the experiment tests whether specialised AI hardware can operate beyond the planet.
items.title: Google Runs AI Model on Satellite Using Onboard Chip

items.summary: The dollar fell against most major currencies on Nov 4 ahead of the US midterm elections, with investors bracing for a potentially strong Democratic showing. The euro firmed to US$1.1212 and the yen strengthened to 158.30 per dollar in early trading. Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said Democrats are favoured to take control of Congress, which could limit government spending over Trump's term and further weaken the dollar.
items.title: Dollar Weakens as US Midterm Results Loom

items.summary: Ahead of Wednesday's US midterm results, Indian markets face potential shifts through trade policy and investor sentiment. Analysts warn the post-election direction matters more than outcomes alone. Ravi Singh at Master Capital Services noted midterms could influence India via tariffs and currency movements, while Ankur Punj advised focusing on domestic earnings rather than political speculation. Initial results arrive early Wednesday as polls close across US time zones.
items.title: Indian investors watch US mid-terms for market impact signals

items.summary: Republican Byron Donalds will become Florida’s next governor and its first Black leader, defeating Democrat David Jolly in a closely watched midterm race. Endorsed by Trump after initially distancing himself, he promises to continue the DeSantis-era agenda while warning against reversal. The seat carries heavy symbolism following eight years of Republican leadership amid rising costs that dominated voter concerns.
items.title: Trump-endorsed Republican Byron Donalds wins Florida race for governor

items.summary: Breakfast cereal maker Kellogg's has stopped using rice grains in Rice Krispies and Coco Pops in the UK, switching to corn flour and rice flour. A spokesperson said the change follows weather conditions disrupting supplies as crops face dry spells across Asia, which produces more than a quarter of the world's rice.
items.title: Kellogg's switches Rice Krispies and Coco Pops away from rice grains in UK

items.summary: Realty firm Prestige Estates Projects Ltd said on Tuesday it acquired 100 per cent equity of Gloind Vintage Infra Pvt Ltd for an enterprise value of ₹519 crore, through its subsidiary Prestige Retail Ventures. The all-cash deal was done from DSFF Series 2 and Jasbir Singh under a Securities Purchase Agreement dated November 3, 2026, making Gloind a wholly owned step-down subsidiary that also controls Tarun Realtors. Prestige Group is described as one of the leading real estate developers in India with presence across major cities.
items.title: Prestige Estates Acquires Full Stake in Gloind Vintage for ₹519 Cr

items.summary: Oil prices fell in early Wednesday trade as investors awaited results of the US midterm elections and their impact on Middle East peace talks. Brent futures dropped 26 cents, or 0.25 per cent, to $103.34 a barrel by 0157 GMT, while WTI crude fell 53 cents, or 0.55 per cent, to $95.56. Crude stocks unexpectedly fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended October 30, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
items.title: Oil Prices Slip as Investors Await US Midterm Election Results

items.summary: Aggregate debt proposed by Indian companies for the current week exceeds Rs 17,000 crore (quantity-133-145) as borrowing conditions stay favorable. The 10-year yield closed at 7. 30% on Tuesday after touching 7. 50% last week (quantities quantity-181-186 and quantity-214-219). Issuers include public sector institutions such as NABARD, REC and SIDBI, plus private firms like Bajaj Housing Finance and Tata Capital Housing Finance. Venkatakrishnan Srinivasan of Rockfort Fincap LLP noted a pile-up of issuances to capitalize on the bond rally. Dipanwita Mazumdar of Bank of Baroda expects benchmark yields to trade between 7. 25% and 7. 35% in November, with upside risks (quantity-1646-1650).
items.title: Indian corporate bond issuers plan record week as yields ease

items.summary: A union representing pathology workers has urged the Queensland state government to intervene as Mater Health prepares to cut around 430 jobs. Mater revealed on Monday that it would outsource pathology services from its hospitals in South Brisbane and Springfield, with more than 100 positions scrapped within two months and most of the remainder ending next year. Together Queensland wrote to Health Minister Tim Nicholls asking him to halt first-phase terminations until consultation is completed. A Mater spokesperson said Medicare funding had not kept pace with rising costs.
items.title: Mater Health Job Cuts Prompt Union Intervention Call

items.summary: Fuel prices across major Indian cities stayed largely stable on November 4, following a Finance Ministry notification that cut petrol export duty to ₹0 per litre from ₹2.50 and raised diesel's levy to ₹11.50 from ₹8.50 per litre as of 31 October. Retail variation stems from local VAT, freight charges, and global oil prices amid Middle East tensions; Brent closed below $104 a barrel while WTI traded near $97.
items.title: Indian Fuel Prices Held Steady After Central Government Duty Cuts

items.summary: Finshots traces how astrology has become a large technology-driven business in India, driven by online platforms connecting astrologers with clients. The industry is estimated to be worth as much as $7 billion, though that figure is not official. AstroTalk, founded in 2017 and recently valued at $1 billion, illustrates the growth; its revenue rose 55% to ₹1,823 crore in FY26, with net profit jumping from ₹22 crore to ₹222 crore. The boom accelerated during the pandemic as users consulted astrologers online, and platforms now also sell gemstones and jewellery while attracting younger customers.
items.title: Astrology's Rise Into India's Billion-Dollar Astrotech Market

items.summary: Two trucks caught fire after a crash at Great Eastern Highway and Quellington Road in Meckering, about 130 kilometres from Perth. The collision involved a refrigerated truck and one towing a container trailer, reported around 6.45am with crews arriving by 7am. A Department of Fire and Emergency Services spokesperson said both vehicles were engulfed when they arrived. It is understood the blaze has since been extinguished.
items.title: Two Trucks Catch Fire After Crash on Western Australia Highway

items.summary: Police officials said Ghanakanta Gogoi, a businessman accused of shooting five people dead at a Guwahati hotel last week, was killed early Wednesday while allegedly trying to escape custody. He was being transported from Guwahati to Sibsagar around 3:12 am in connection with a separate case when the incident occurred.
items.title: Man accused of Guwahati hotel killings shot dead in police encounter

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge to submit responses to a petition questioning their role in the October 12 march into the court complex. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the matter for November 23, asking the Centre and private respondents to file replies. Petition lawyer Gaurav Bhatia alleged that Gandhi pushed an injured pregnant journalist during the gathering. Respondent advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi said a response would be filed.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Gandhi, Kharge Responses Over October 12 March

items.summary: In the 2026 US midterm elections, Democrats gained early ground as polls closed across states. Democrat Roy Cooper flipped North Carolina's open Senate seat over Republican Michael Whatley, with CBS News reporting he secured 1,501,539 votes (66.8%) at 56% of ballots counted. Democrats also lead in New Hampshire and Virginia races, adding to a closely watched contest for the balance of power in Congress.
items.title: Democrats Flip North Carolina Senate Seat in Midterm Upset

items.summary: The first midterm votes counted Tuesday night suggest a difficult night for Republicans, consistent with polling placing Democrats ahead on frustration with President Donald Trump’s agenda. In Indiana and Kentucky, where polls closed at 6 pm ET, Democrats led their early totals two years ago. Both seats saw later investment as the environment worsened for Republicans; House Majority PAC spent nearly $400,000 in Indiana while a green energy group backed its opponent. Democrats remain cautious about overreading early returns after losing ground on Election Day previously.
items.title: Early Midterm Votes Show Democrats Ahead in Indiana and Kentucky

items.summary: On Tuesday night, Democrats won three open Senate seats—Georgia's Jon Ossoff, New Hampshire's Chris Pappas, and North Carolina's Roy Cooper—as House Republicans also lost Florida districts. Columnist David noted the early returns looked like a repudiation of Trump his party had not seen in 2020. Yet Democrats remain wary of overreading early votes after losing ground to Kamala Harris supporters on Election Day two years ago.
items.title: Democrats Gain Senate Seats as Republicans Underperform in Midterms

items.summary: Anita Devi began growing mushrooms in Anantpur, Nalanda district, Bihar, in 2010 after officials at the Krishi Vigyan Kendra suggested cultivation. Initially mocked by villagers who called it gobar chatta, she continued and established a farmers' company in 2016 to help women access support and markets. Nearly 250 women had joined the Madhopur Farmers Producers Company Limited by December 2017, with Devi earning more than Rs 25,000 monthly in 2017. A 2025 Farmland Bazaar report says the company expanded to 512 farmers, targeting 1,500. On March 8, 2025, she shared her story through Prime Minister Narendra Modi's social media accounts on International Women's Day and considered expanding into makhana production.
items.title: Bihar Woman Turns Village Into Mushroom Enterprise Empowering Hundreds of Women

items.summary: Bharat Sisodia, a tree-transplantation expert in Ahmedabad, found that a nearly 100-year-old peepal had been felled for road development, leaving only about six to seven feet of trunk. He and his team dug around the stump, brought in a 50-tonne crane, and moved it roughly two kilometres before replanting it with soil treatments and nutrients. The tree reportedly shows new growth, though Sisodia warns it could be cut down again amid development plans tied to hosting major games. As reported by The Better India, his approach—‘plantenance’—emphasises long-term care over one-time planting.
items.title: Tree expert relocates century-old peepal after it was cut down

items.summary: Counting began after voting closed on Tuesday (November 3) in the US mid-term elections, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency. Partial House and Senate tallies were already emerging by late evening into Wednesday (November 4), with polls predicting Democratic gains.
items.title: US Mid-Term Polls Counting Begins as Results Awaited

items.summary: The Union Centre has asked the Delhi High Court to remove a century-old mosque, Qadeemi Masjid, from within the Krishi Bhawan complex in New Delhi as part of its Central Vista redevelopment. The Centre argues that retaining it is impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property. Its caretaking committee contends the mosque predates Independence, citing records dating back to 1945 and a November 8, 1940 agreement granting permissive use but not ownership. The court must weigh these claims as redevelopment proceeds.
items.title: Centre Seeks Removal of Krishi Bhawan Mosque Over Central Vista Redevelopment

items.summary: Several flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats Tuesday, prompting searches, diversions and an Italian Air Force escort until landing, officials said. Affected carriers included LOT, Scandinavian Airlines (SAS), Wizz Air and Ryanair; no one was injured. In Italy a Ryanair flight from Lisbon landed in Rome after an email reported a bomb on board, with police finding nothing. A Polish LOT flight diverted to Modlin Airport also found nothing aboard. Bulgaria ruled out explosives on two aircraft at Sofia, while authorities still sought the threat's sender. Matthew Borie of Osprey Flight Solutions offered hypotheses including copycat incidents and possible hybrid warfare by state actors.
items.title: European Flights Diverted After Coordinated Bomb Threat Hoax

items.summary: A major fire broke out in the kitchen area of Kings Restaurant near Mehdipatnam X Roads in Hyderabad in the early hours of Wednesday. Huge flames suddenly erupted, triggering concern among locals. Fire personnel rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control. No casualties have been reported so far.
items.title: Fire Breaks Out at Kings Restaurant in Mehdipatnam

items.summary: India's real estate market is moving beyond festive discounts, freebies and promotional schemes toward a more discerning buyer focused on fundamentals. Demand spans premium housing, larger configurations, plotted developments and flexible office spaces in both residential and commercial segments. Developers are offering benefits such as stamp-duty support, parking waivers and structured payment plans like 10:90 and construction-linked payments. Notandas Realty's Harsh Jagwani estimates the premium segment could grow 20-30 per cent during the festive season. Micro Mitti's Manoj Dhanotiya warns investors to assess intrinsic value rather than discounts, while Krisumi Corporation reports fivefold sales growth amid rising interest in overseas brands.
items.title: Indian Real Estate Shifts Toward Premium Homes and Flexible Payments

items.summary: The U.S. Army has signed a nonbinding term sheet with REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) proposing an initial 50-year lease, possibly extended by 25 years, on roughly 200 acres at Tooele Army Depot in Utah to build and operate heavy rare earth processing for dysprosium and terbium. The deal would let the Army exercise a right of first offer without any obligation to buy, while REalloys funds construction and operations. It aims to reduce dependence on China, which controls most global processing after April 2025 export restrictions. Retired General Jack Keane called it an important step toward U.S.-controlled supply chains. The term sheet is nonbinding; finalizing requires financing, environmental reviews and regulatory approvals before a January 1, 2027 federal sourcing deadline.
items.title: Army and REalloys Sign Nonbinding Term Sheet for Rare Earth Facility
